exercises.title: Bài 1 · Types of e-commerce
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
E-commerce means buying and selling goods or services over the internet. Today, it is growing fast in almost every country, and many people are shopping more on their phones than on computers. There are several business models.

In B2C, a business sells to individual consumers, for example a fashion store with its own website. In B2B, a company sells to other companies, usually in larger quantities and at wholesale prices. In C2C, consumers sell to each other on a marketplace, such as a second-hand clothing platform. A newer model is D2C, in which a brand skips retailers and sells directly to the customer, so it keeps more of the profit and owns the customer data.

Business owners also choose how to run their stores. A marketplace gives instant access to millions of buyers, but it charges a commission and limits control of the brand. An own online store is more expensive to build, but it gives full control. Some start-ups use dropshipping, so they do not keep any stock; the supplier ships the product directly to the buyer. Others offer a subscription model, which creates a regular revenue stream.

content.q: E-commerce is declining in most countries.
content.why: Đoạn 1: thương mại điện tử đang **tăng nhanh** ở hầu hết các nước.

content.q: In C2C, consumers sell to each other.
In D2C, a brand sells directly to the customer.
content.why: Đoạn 2: thương hiệu bỏ qua nhà bán lẻ và bán thẳng.

content.q: A marketplace gives sellers full control of their brand.
content.why: Đoạn 3: sàn **hạn chế** quyền kiểm soát thương hiệu.

content.q: What does a D2C brand keep?
content.why: Đoạn 2: giữ nhiều lợi nhuận hơn và sở hữu dữ liệu khách hàng.
opts: More of the profit and the customer data

content.q: What is an advantage of a marketplace?
content.why: Đoạn 3: tiếp cận ngay hàng triệu người mua.
opts: Instant access to millions of buyers

content.q: What does the seller do in dropshipping?
content.why: Đoạn 3: nhà cung cấp gửi hàng thẳng cho người mua.
opts: Does not keep stock; the supplier ships directly

content.q: What does a subscription model create?
content.why: Đoạn 3: nguồn doanh thu đều đặn.

Linh is a 26-year-old graphic designer, and she is opening an online store that sells handmade leather bags. She is targeting a small niche: customers who want unique, high-quality products. Right now she is deciding between a marketplace and her own website.

After comparing both options, Linh decides to do both. She lists three best-selling bags on the marketplace to find new customers, and she is building her own storefront for her complete product range. "The marketplace brings traffic," she says, "but my website builds my brand." Next month, she plans to sell on social media, too. Her goal is to earn 30% of her revenue from repeat customers within a year.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · What makes a good product page?
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A product page is where a visitor decides to buy or leave, so every detail matters. First, the product images should be large and clear, and customers should be able to zoom in and see the product from several angles. A short video can help, too. Second, the product description must explain the main features and benefits in simple words. For clothes and shoes, a size guide reduces returns.

Customer reviews and ratings are also important, because shoppers trust other buyers more than the brand. The page should show the price, the delivery cost and the stock status clearly, so there are no surprises at checkout. Finally, a clear call to action, such as a bright 'Add to cart' button, tells the visitor what to do next.

Designers also think about page speed and responsive design. If a page loads slowly, many visitors leave before they see anything. Since most visits come from phones, the layout must work well on small screens. Good user experience, in the end, means that customers find what they need quickly and feel confident to buy.

content.why: Đoạn 1: khách nên có thể phóng to hình ảnh.

content.q: A size guide increases returns.
content.why: Đoạn 1: bảng size giúp **giảm** trả hàng.

content.q: Shoppers trust other buyers more than the brand.
Slow pages do not affect visitors.
content.why: Đoạn 3: trang chậm khiến nhiều khách **rời đi**.

content.q: What should the product description explain?
content.why: Đoạn 1: tính năng và lợi ích chính.

content.q: Why should the page show the delivery cost and stock status clearly?
content.why: Đoạn 2: để không có bất ngờ khi thanh toán.

content.q: What does a clear call to action do?

content.q: What does good user experience mean?
content.why: Đoạn 3: khách tìm được thứ cần nhanh và tự tin mua.

On Monday, the web team met to discuss why many visitors left the website without buying. Hoa, the UX designer, showed a report: 60% of visitors left on the checkout page, and the average loading time on mobile was six seconds.

Hoa suggested simplifying the checkout. At the moment, customers must create an account, fill in twelve fields and accept three pop-ups. She recommended that the team offer a guest checkout and reduce the number of fields to six. Minh, the developer, said that they could compress the images to improve page speed. He thought that the loading time might fall to three seconds.

Lan, the marketing manager, proposed adding trust badges and a live chat button, because customers often ask about delivery and returns before they pay. Everybody agreed, but the head of the team, Mr Son, asked whether they should test the changes first. They decided to run an A/B test for two weeks, and Hoa will share the results at the next meeting.

content.why: Đoạn 1: thời gian tải là **sáu giây**; ba giây là mục tiêu.

content.q: Hoa recommended offering a guest checkout.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · How online payments work
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
When a customer clicks "Pay now", a lot happens in a few seconds. First, the website sends the order total and the payment details to a payment gateway. The gateway encrypts the data, so hackers cannot read it, and passes it to the payment processor. The processor contacts the customer's bank, which checks whether the card is valid and whether there is enough money. Many banks also send a one-time password to the customer's phone. If everything is correct, the payment is approved and the customer sees an order confirmation. If it fails, the payment is declined, and the customer can try another payment method.

Online stores usually offer several methods: credit and debit cards, e-wallets, bank transfers, QR code payments and, in many countries, cash on delivery. Some also provide buy now, pay later or an instalment plan, which makes a high price easier to accept.

Each method has a cost. Processors charge a transaction fee, often a percentage of the sale, and the seller receives the money later as a payout. Offering more payment methods usually increases sales, because customers can pay in the way they prefer.

content.q: The gateway encrypts the payment data.
content.why: Đoạn 1: cổng thanh toán mã hóa dữ liệu.

content.q: The seller receives the money instantly with no fees.
content.why: Đoạn 3: có **transaction fee** và tiền về sau dưới dạng payout.

content.q: A declined payment means the customer cannot try again.
content.why: Đoạn 1: khách có thể **thử phương thức khác**.

content.q: Offering more payment methods usually increases sales.

One Saturday morning, Linh's online shop received twelve orders for expensive handbags within ten minutes. All of them used different credit cards, but the shipping address was the same. The fraud detection system raised an alert, and Linh put the orders on hold.

If an order looks suspicious, the shop follows a simple procedure. First, the team checks whether the billing address matches the card. Then it calls the customer or sends an email to verify the order. If the customer does not reply within 24 hours, the order is cancelled and the payment is refunded. In this case, nobody answered, so Linh cancelled all twelve orders.

Two weeks later, she was glad that she had acted quickly. Another seller on the platform had shipped similar orders and later received twelve chargebacks, which means that the banks took the money back from his account. He also had to pay a fee for each chargeback, and his payment processor reviewed his account.

Since then, Linh has introduced stronger security: she requires an OTP for large orders, and she uses a secure checkout with an SSL certificate and tokenisation. "It costs a little more," she says, "but one chargeback costs much more."

To sell online, a shop first needs visitors. There are two main ways to get them: organic and paid. Organic traffic comes from search engines when people type a keyword and click a result. When a customer clicks "Place order", the fulfilment process starts. First, the order is sent to the warehouse, and the system checks the stock level. If the item is in stock, a worker picks it from the shelf. In a large fulfilment centre, this is done by scanners and sometimes by robots. If the item is out of stock, it may be put on backorder until the shop can restock.

Next, the item is packed. Good packaging protects the product and does not waste material. A shipping label with the address and a tracking number is attached to the parcel, and a delivery note is placed inside. The parcel is then handed to a courier, and the customer receives an email with the tracking number.

The final stage, last-mile delivery, is the most expensive part of the journey, because the courier must visit many different addresses. Customers can choose express shipping or a delivery slot, but these options usually cost more. After the parcel is delivered, a proof of delivery, such as a signature or a photo, is recorded. If the customer decides to return the goods, reverse logistics takes over, and the product is checked, repaired or restocked.

exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Every online shop receives complaints about late delivery, defective products or wrong items. The way a company responds can decide whether the customer stays or leaves. Good customer service follows four steps. First, listen and apologise: "I'm sorry to hear that your parcel arrived damaged." Show empathy and avoid blaming the customer. Second, find the facts by asking for the order number and a photo. Third, offer a resolution quickly, such as a replacement, an exchange or a refund. If the shop is responsible for the problem, it may add a goodwill gesture, such as a voucher. Finally, follow up to check that the customer is happy.

Companies also measure their service. Response time shows how fast agents answer, and the CSAT score shows how satisfied customers are after a ticket is closed. The NPS shows how likely customers are to recommend the shop.

A knowledge base and canned responses help agents to answer faster, but the tone of voice should still be friendly and personal. Companies that handle problems well keep more customers, so they have a lower churn rate.

exercises.passage:
Online shops produce a huge amount of data every day. Analytics tools show how many sessions a site had, where visitors came from and which pages they visited. One important figure is the bounce rate: the percentage of visitors who leave after seeing only one page. A high bounce rate may mean that the page is too slow or that the product is not what visitors expected.

Managers also follow the conversion funnel: visitors view a product, add it to the cart, start the checkout and finally pay. At each step, some people leave. Abandoned carts are especially important, because the customer already wanted to buy. A reminder email can recover part of those sales.

Other metrics measure money. The average order value shows how much customers spend in one order. The customer acquisition cost shows how much it costs to win a new customer, while the customer lifetime value shows how much that customer will spend over time. A healthy shop has a lifetime value that is much higher than the acquisition cost. Finally, A/B testing compares two versions of a page, so teams can decide with evidence, not opinion.

exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
During last year's 11.11 sale, an online fashion shop expected 20,000 visitors an hour. Instead, 80,000 arrived in the first hour, and the site was so slow that most customers could not complete their orders. After 25 minutes, the website crashed completely. The uptime for the month fell to 98.9%, and the shop lost an estimated 2 billion dong in sales.

The problem was not the products or the discounts, but the technology. The shop used a cheap hosting plan that was not strong enough to handle peak traffic. Also, the team had never tested the system with a large number of users. If it had done a load test, it would have found the weakness earlier. Moreover, the payment plug-in and the inventory system were not well integrated through the API, so stock levels were wrong and some customers bought items that did not exist.

After the crash, the shop moved to cloud hosting with auto-scaling, which adds servers when traffic rises. It also installed a dashboard that shows real-time data and sends an alert if the page speed falls. This year, the shop ran load tests two weeks before the sale. "If we had prepared last year, we would have kept our customers," the CTO said.

The site crashed after 25 minutes.
content.why: Đoạn 1: sau 25 phút trang web sập hoàn toàn.

content.why: Đoạn 2: đội **chưa từng** kiểm thử với số lượng lớn.

content.q: The shop moved to cloud hosting afterwards.
content.why: Đoạn 3: chuyển sang lưu trữ đám mây có tự động mở rộng.

content.q: What was the main problem?
content.why: Đoạn 2: gói hosting rẻ không đủ mạnh khi lưu lượng cao điểm.

content.why: Đoạn 2: hệ thống tồn kho và plug-in thanh toán không được tích hợp tốt qua API.

content.why: Đoạn 3: tự thêm máy chủ khi lưu lượng tăng.
opts: It adds servers when traffic rises

content.q: What did the CTO say?
content.why: Đoạn 3: nếu chuẩn bị từ năm ngoái thì đã giữ được khách.

E-commerce is creating many new jobs. In a typical online company, an e-commerce manager is responsible for the whole business: sales targets, the website and the marketing plan. A category manager looks after a group of products and decides which items to sell and at what price. Digital marketers run campaigns, and copywriters write product descriptions and advertisements. Other roles include data analysts, customer service agents, warehouse supervisors and logistics coordinators.

The work depends on seasons. Peak season usually starts in autumn, with events such as Singles' Day and Black Friday, and the teams prepare for months. A campaign calendar shows the dates of promotions, and every team has KPI targets, such as sales, conversion rate or response time. During the peak, people often work long hours, so planning and teamwork are essential.

Skills are changing, too. Employers want people who can use data, understand digital marketing and communicate clearly in English with suppliers and customers from other countries. Many professionals start in customer service or in a warehouse, learn how the business works and then move into management. Whatever the role, curiosity and the willingness to learn new tools are very important.
